notes: Missing why single-threaded execution is fast (no lock contention / context switching); single thread is only described, not justified. Correctly notes 6.0 optional I/O threads; all quotes verified.

All must_cover present and no AOF-never-loses claim. Three key points carry sub-claims absent from their own quotes (KP3 'lose at most ~1s', KP4 background rewrite, KP5 'RDB alone if minutes of loss OK'); all are on the cited page, so 0 unsupported claims.

Levels and RR default covered, but read phenomena are not mapped per level (non-repeatable read never named; what RR/SERIALIZABLE prevent is left implicit). RU described as 'reading an earlier row version = dirty read' (doc wording, misleading in an interview); KP2 'locks only index records' not in its quote; SET TRANSACTION detail is padding.

One-per-table and secondary-index lookback via PK covered; 'rows stored in PK order in the clustered index leaf nodes' is never stated, only inferred from the generic B-tree leaf-page point. Quotes all verified; '6-byte row ID' in short answer is on the cited page.
Covers SYN / SYN+ACK / ACK, ISN synchronization and the old-duplicate rationale, all quoted from RFC 9293. No issues.

All points covered; memory point is MDN's 'unnecessary nested functions cost memory' rather than retained references, acceptable. KP4's 'gets the last value' and 'function factory fix' are on the page but not in its quotes.
Missing the call stack entirely; task queue, microtask draining after each task and rendering timing are covered. No setTimeout-runs-immediately claim; quotes verified.
All must_cover present and correctly says key is not passed as a prop. KP2's 'index keys cause bugs on insert/delete/reorder' is on the page but not in its quotes.
Smallest deployable unit, shared network/storage, workload-resource management and ephemerality all covered and quoted. No issues.

Covers framing, multiplexing, HPACK, flow control/priority (with correct note that RFC 9113 deprecates RFC 7540 priority signaling) and TCP HOL caveat. KP3 'incrementally updated header table' is on RFC 7541 but not in the quotes; priority/flow control coverage is thin.
